_comment: Mars orbit the crew picks in the designer (SHIP column). Read by scripts/orbits.gd. FIRST-GUESS numbers (SIMPLIFIED), tune with humans. moi_mult scales the mission's moi_fuel; science_mult / contact_mult scale science observed / data sent per Mars year in orbit; drag = fuel % spent per Mars year keeping the orbit; delay_years = time before science starts (aerobraking). Facts: Odyssey aerobraked 77 days (332 passes) to a ~400 km near-polar orbit, mapping from Feb 2002; MRO aerobraked ~5 months (2006) to ~250-316 km; MAVEN maps between ~150 and ~6,200 km.

low.name: LOW POLAR
low.desc: Close up: sharp pictures of the whole planet. But a BIG brake burn, Earth often hidden behind Mars, and drag costs fuel every year.
low.real: Odyssey and MRO map Mars from low polar orbits.

elliptical.name: HIGH ELLIPTICAL
elliptical.desc: Small brake burn. Far from Mars most of the time: long talks with Earth, little drag, long life - but fewer close looks.
elliptical.real: MAVEN flies 150 x 6,200 km to sample the air at every height.

aerobrake.name: AEROBRAKE
aerobrake.desc: Small brake, then hundreds of dips through the air lower the orbit. Low-orbit science for little fuel, but months of waiting.
aerobrake.real: MRO aerobraked about 5 months, Odyssey 77 days.

radiator.why: radiator kept the ship cool through the hot dips

solar_large.why: big solar wings acted as drag brakes, like MRO's
